## 1. Scope and evidence

Derived from one fleet run: 51 subagent transcripts, 1,315 tool calls (deduped by
`tool_use` block id), 1,145 assistant messages (deduped by `message.id`). Session logs,
exact paths, and the per-agent file map are in
[fleet-run-token-accounting.md §1](./fleet-run-token-accounting.md#1-source-evidence).

Session: `76327173-6061-4d25-bdd9-8b785c49c7e7`. Run cost $114.55 API-equivalent for two
tasks. Source inspected at `plugins/wf/0.79.0` and `plugins/wf-audit/0.1.7` as installed;
line numbers below refer to that state.

## 3. Defects

### D0 — `/ship` has no orchestrator-side context management

**Recoverable: ~$10 of $33.67 spent.** The single largest cost in the run, and not a
discrete leak — it is unbounded accumulation.

**Evidence.** `agent-ab005bb4b6451f1d9.jsonl` (Ship SM-2): 174 messages, context grew
43K -> **422K**, 24.0M cache read, $20.26 from one agent.
`agent-a76528da96be9da00.jsonl` (Ship SM-3): $13.41. Together 31% of subagent spend.

**Code.** `plugins/wf/skills/ship/SKILL.md` contains no compaction, hand-off, or
context-budget step — grepping compact/context/handoff returns only lines 50 and 76, both
about phase sequencing. Line 50 compounds it: ship drives `/wf:branch`, `/wf:run`,
`/wf:pr`, `/wf:tf` **through the Skill tool**, i.e. inline in its own context. `/wf:run`
isolates its phases into subagents, but pr/tf and every handoff summary accumulate in the
shipper.

**Direction.** Give ship a context budget — compact, or hand off to a fresh shipper,
at ~150K.

---

### D1 — audit lenses read whole files, and five of them read the same ones

**Recoverable: ~$11 of $18.65, with a quality tradeoff.**

**Evidence.** 15 lens agents issued 117 Reads totalling 971.9K chars — 768.6K of it (79%)
re-reading a file another agent had already read. `server.ts` read 22x across 16 agents;
`app.ts` 15x across 11. Meanwhile **only 4 `git diff`/`git show` calls exist across all 51
agents, averaging 74 chars** — the auditors never worked from a diff; they read entire
source files.

**Code.** `plugins/wf/skills/verify-spec/SKILL.md:220-222` spawns each `finding` fragment
whose dispatch is `subagent` via the Task tool, "passing the artifact under audit and the
generic finding shape" — a *pointer*, not content. Each auditor then Reads/Greps the files
itself.

**Mechanism — important.** The cross-agent duplication is **not recoverable by
deduplication.** Five isolated agents each need the content in their own context; it
cannot be shared, and inlining the *same bytes* into five prompts saves nothing. Only two
things actually save:

1. **Collapse 5 lenses -> 1 agent with 5 rubric sections.** Saves 4x content + 4 boots,
   ~$11. Costs five independent perspectives that cannot anchor on each other, plus
   parallelism. A quality/latency tradeoff, not a free win.
2. **Pass changed hunks instead of whole files.** Saves only to the extent the diff is
   smaller than the files. Given the near-total absence of diff calls this is **untested
   here** — measure before committing.

---

### D2 — model selection is one level deep

**Recoverable: ~$11 (lens + bookkeeping + qa on sonnet); ~$18 if verify is included, but
that is judgment-heavy and riskier.**

**Evidence.** All 51 agents ran `claude-opus-4-8`, including 10 bookkeeping agents and 15
lenses.

**Code.** `plugins/wf/skills/fleet/SKILL.md:206` — "The shipper model is set per dispatch
via the Agent tool's `model` field." No agent file under `plugins/wf/agents/` or
`plugins/wf-audit/agents/` declares `model:` in frontmatter, so everything a shipper spawns
inherits the shipper's model. There is no way to express "ship on opus, run lenses and
bookkeeping on sonnet."

> **Refuted sub-theory.** The `**Model:** claude-opus-4-8` line at the foot of the auditor
> agent files is the **Core-Article-4 attribution line**, not a model selector. An earlier
> reading called it a hardcoded pin. It is not.

**Direction.** Declare `model:` in frontmatter for the mechanical agents (index, classify,
branch), or have callers pass `model` explicitly on the Task call.

---

### D6 — `wf:index` runs as a subagent to write one table row

**Recoverable: ~$3.** 10 bookkeeping agents, ~9 messages and 55–80K `cache_creation` each,
to edit a table row. Instruction at
`plugins/wf/skills/verify-spec/SKILL.md:256` and the same pattern across the other skills.
20% of the agent count for 3% of the cost.

**Direction.** Single-row index edits belong in the caller's context.

---

### D5 — shell idiom collides with host guardrails

**Recoverable: ~$2. Attribution is mostly a guidance gap, not emitted commands.**

**Evidence.** 50 of 481 Bash calls (10.4%) returned `BLOCKED` — 25 cat/head/tail, 16 `cd`,
6 pipes, 2 `&&`/`;`, 1 redirection. Each wastes a round trip that re-reads the agent's
whole context on retry (~50 x ~85K ≈ $2).

**Code.** The blocked calls are overwhelmingly the *model* reaching for POSIX idioms
(`cd X && git …`, `ls | head`) — the shipper prompt template never tells subagents the
constraint exists. Only the build/test subset traces to plugin text:
`plugins/wf/skills/init/SKILL.md:108-123` templates `(cd <dir> && npm run <script>)` into
the consuming project's `_testkit`.

**Direction.** Add shell constraints to the shipper prompt template; emit
`npm --prefix <dir> run <script>` in the init template. Note this is host-dependent — the
guardrail is the user's hook, not universal.

---

### D4 — every lens re-fetches the shared contract

**Recoverable: <$0.5, but free to fix.** `fragments/finding-contract.md` fetched 15x by 15
distinct agents (46.4K chars); each lens makes 2 resolver round trips (contract + own
rubric) before doing any work. Instruction is explicit at line 23 of all five auditor
files in `plugins/wf-audit/agents/`. `resolve_content` overall: 266.6K chars, 156.2K
duplicated.

**Direction.** The contract is static — inline it into the dispatch prompt.

---

### D7 — intra-agent repeat reads

**Recoverable: <$0.5.** 23 cases of one agent re-reading a file 2–4x, 63.7K chars. Worst:
the SM-3 verify-spec re-run (`agent-adc226019ad2d7b92.jsonl`) read `04_verify.md` 4x
(36K chars), suggesting the rotate-to-`.history.md` step
(`plugins/wf/skills/verify-spec/SKILL.md:241-243`) leaves the agent re-reading the report
it just rotated. Partly model behaviour rather than plugin design.

---

### D3 — the lens gate is applied after the agent has booted

**Latent — $0 in this run, but bites exactly when someone gates lenses off to save
tokens.**

**Code.** `plugins/wf-audit/agents/correctness-auditor.md` procedure: step 1 fetches
`fragments/finding-contract.md` through the resolver; step 2 then says "Apply the profile
lens-gate for lens id `correctness`. If gated off, emit ... clean ... and stop." A disabled
lens therefore still costs a full agent spawn (~20K `cache_creation` boot) plus an MCP
round trip to produce a no-op. All five auditor agents share this ordering.

**Direction.** Evaluate the gate caller-side, before dispatch.

---

### D8 — the resolver loads every tool schema into every context

**A different axis from D0–D7: fixed per-context boot overhead, not per-run agent spend.**
Every context that boots the resolver — the main session and *each* of the 51 subagents in
the measured run — carried all 20 resolver tool schemas.

**Evidence — measured directly from the server, not inferred.** Driving the shipped bundle
through an MCP `initialize` + `tools/list` handshake and summing `JSON.stringify(tool)` per
advertised tool:

| | tools | chars | est. tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| before (blanket `alwaysLoad: true`) | 20 | 32,330 | ~8,083 |
| after (per-tool residency) | 5 | 18,011 | ~4,503 |
| **deferred** | **15** | **14,509** | **~3,627 (45%)** |

`resolve_routing` alone is 12,924 chars (~3,231 tokens) — 40% of the pre-change total.

**Mechanism.** The host defers every MCP tool by default; a tool is resident only if the
server config sets `alwaysLoad` **or** the tool carries `_meta["anthropic/alwaysLoad"]`.
`plugins/wf/.mcp.json` set the blanket server-level flag, so nothing deferred.

**Which 15 defer — chosen on skill-body references, not call frequency.** Counting files
under `plugins/*/skills` and `plugins/*/agents` that name each op gives a clean cliff:
`resolve_content` 57, `resolve_config` 46, `resolve_provider` 36, `resolve_routing` 26,
`resolve_registry` 25 — then `resolve_gate` 18 (but **zero** calls in a 50-transcript
window: a failure-path gate), `register_pack`/`inspect_pack` 18 (one-time pack onboarding),
`resolve_profile` 9, and the rest ≤5. The top five stay resident; the other 15 cost one
tool-search round trip on the rare paths that reach them.

**Two risks this change does NOT retire — both need a live install to settle.**

1. **Blocking vs non-blocking connect.** The server-level flag also placed the server on the
   host's *blocking* startup-connect path. Per-tool `_meta` recovers schema residency but
   **not** connect ordering, so the resolver now connects non-blocking. Skills call
   `resolve_config` as their first step, so a slow cold start could in principle be reached
   before the server is ready.
2. **The C011 prompt-free claim.** [content-read-call-site-inventory.md
   §OUT-1](./content-read-call-site-inventory.md) argued an unattended `run --auto` pass is
   prompt-free partly *because* the server was `alwaysLoad`. The tool-use grant is keyed to
   the tool name rather than to schema residency, and `resolve_content` stays resident
   either way — but that doc itself notes CI cannot drive a real `run --auto`, so this is
   reasoned, not measured.

**Recoverable dollars: not estimated.** The saving is per-context boot tokens, which land in
`cache_creation`/`cache_read` rather than in the per-agent output spend D0–D7 are ranked by.
Converting 3,627 tokens × N contexts into dollars requires a re-measured fleet run under
[§2's method](./fleet-run-token-accounting.md#2-method--and-the-trap); until then this row
states tokens only, per §5.

Recorded so they are not re-investigated.

**D-N1 — "the plan skill is too thin, forcing implement to re-explore."** Refuted.
`02_plan.md` maxes at **31,177 chars**, nearly double the spec (16,042) — not thin. Most of
implement's re-reading is structurally forced: the Edit tool requires a prior Read of any
file it modifies. For SM-3 (`agent-a105765e790518bc3.jsonl`), **82%** of re-read volume was
on files it mutated. And `plugins/wf/skills/plan/SKILL.md:149-151` *deliberately* excludes
code ("No exact code — describe the change in plain language"), so the plan cannot
eliminate implement's file reads by construction. The plan->implement clear is working as
designed.

Residue worth one look, not a defect: SM-2's implement
(`agent-a24d59cc01e8dff8c.jsonl`) spent **50.5K chars on consult-only files** it never
mutated (`main.mjs`, `mcp-app.ts`, `test-bundle.mjs`), vs SM-3's 15.2K. That asymmetry —
45% forced for SM-2 vs 82% for SM-3 — may indicate the plan is under-specified for
port-style tasks, or simply caution about unfamiliar code. The evidence cannot separate
those.

**D-N2 — "auditor agent files hardcode opus."** Refuted; see the note under [D2](#d2--model-selection-is-one-level-deep).

---

## 5. Change control

This inventory is the reviewed baseline for a **single** fleet run (n=2 tasks). Ratios are
suggestive, not established. A newly discovered leak — or a re-measurement that moves a
ranking — requires an explicit update here with its evidence, not silent revision.

Before adding a row, re-read
[fleet-run-token-accounting.md §2](./fleet-run-token-accounting.md#2-method--and-the-trap).
Numbers produced without the `message.id` dedup are wrong by roughly 2x and are not
admissible.
